<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="41.186.68.181" /></noinclude><section begin="par47" />ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}} of nouns, and of the 3rd fem. sing. perfect. For the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} {{GHGheb|text=(וּן)}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}, see {{GHGpar|47|c|nonumber=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|e}}
'''3.''' The characteristic vowel of the second syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before tone-bearing afformatives which begin with a vowel, but is retained (as being in the tone-syllable) before the toneless afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}. Thus: {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלִ֫י}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְל֫וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְל֫וּ}} (but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לִי}} &c.), {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|f}}
Rem. 1. The ''ō'' of the second syllable (as in the inf. constr. and imperat.), being lengthened from an original ''ŭ'' in the tone-syllable, is only tone-long ({{GHGpar|9|r}}). Hence it follows that: (''a'') it is incorrectly, although somewhat frequently, written {{GHGterm|plene}}; (''b'') before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} the short vowel appears as {{GHGterm|Qameṣ ḥaṭuph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּכְתָּב־שָּׁם|translate=and he wrote there}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=32}} (but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=20}}); (''c'') it becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before the tone-bearing afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} (see above, e; but Jerome still heard e.g. ''iezbuleni'' for {{GHGheb|text=יִזְבְּלֵ֫נִי}}; cf. {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} iv. 83).

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|g}}
Quite anomalous are the three examples which, instead of a shortening to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, exhibit a long ''û'': {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁפּוּטוּ הֵֽם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=26}}, immediately before the principal pause, but according to Qimḥi (ed. ''Rittenb''. p.18<sup>b</sup>), ed. Mant., Ginsb., Kittel against the other editions, with the tone on the ultima; likewise {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־תַֽעֲבוּרִ֖י מִוֶּה֑}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם}} (in principal pause) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=3}}. In the first two cases perhaps {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁפּ֫וֹטוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּעֲב֫וֹרִי}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁפֹּ֫טוּ}}, &c.) are intended, in virtue of a retrogressive effect of the pause; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁמְרוּם}} is to be read, with August Müller.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|h}}
2. The ''ō'' of the second syllable is to be found almost exclusively with transitive verbs middle ''a'', like {{GHGheb|text=קָטַל}}. Intransitives ''middle a'' and ''ē'' almost always take ''ă'' ({{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}})<ref>This ''ă'' is, however, by no means restricted to intransitive ''strong'' verbs; apart from verbs third guttural ({{GHGpar|65|b}}), it is to be found in {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, and in many verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} and {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} (§§ 69–71).</ref> in the impf., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רָבַץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִרְבַּץ|translate=to couch}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁכַּב|translate=to lie down}} ({{GHGheb|text=לָמַד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִלְמַד|translate=to learn}} is also originally intransitive = ''to accustom oneself''); {{GHGheb|text=גָּדֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִגְדַּל|translate=to become great}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַן}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכֵן}} imperf. {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁכֹּן|translate=to dwell}} and ''to inhabit'', {{GHGheb|text=נָבֵל}} imperf. {{GHGheb|text=יִבֹּל|translate=to wither}}); also from verbs ''middle ō'', as {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹן|translate=to be small}}, the imperf. has the form {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטַן}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|i}}
Sometimes both forms occur together; those with ''ō'' having a transitive, and those with ''ă'' an intransitive meaning, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְצֹר|translate=he cuts off}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקְצַר|translate=he is cut off}}, i.e. ''is short''; {{GHGheb|text=חָלַשׁ}} impf. ''ō'', ''to overcome'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=13}}; impf. ''ă'', ''to be overcome'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=10}}. More rarely both forms are used without any distinction, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִשֹּׁךְ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִשַּׁךְ|translate=he bites}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְפַּץ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יַחְפֹּץ|translate=he is inclined}} (but only the latter with a transitive meaning=''he bends'', in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=17}}). On the ''a'' of the impf. of verbs middle and third guttural, cf. {{GHGpar|64|b}}; {{GHGpar|65|b}}. In some verbs first guttural ({{GHGpar|63|n}}), {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|p}}), {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} ({{GHGpar|69|b}}), and {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} ({{GHGpar|68|c}}), and in {{GHGheb|text=יִתֵּן}} for ''yintēn'' from {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן|translate=to give}}, instead of ''ă'' or ''ō'' a movable {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} (originally ''ĭ'') is found in the second syllable. A trace of these ''i''-imperfects<ref>Cf. Barth, ‘Das ĭ-Imperfekt im Nordsemitischen,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1889, p. 177 ff.</ref> in the ordinary strong verb is probably to be found in {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּטְמִ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}, since {{GHGheb|text=טמן}} otherwise only occurs in Qal. We call these three forms of the imperfect after their characteristic vowel impf. ''o'', impf. ''a'', impf. ''e''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|k}}
